key_risks.title: Arbol climate ≠ availability
key_risks.body: Beazley discloses two non-damage products (trigger_gap 2/4, product_fit 2/4) — parametric climate risk management via Arbol coverholder and kWh Analytics renewable covers. Index triggers capture weather and generation shortfall, not NESO gate status or distribution curtailment — UK wind, solar and BESS cedants on Syndicate 623/2623 may still face basis risk on grid-firmness revenue loss despite clearest parametric build-out in batch4.

key_risks.title: kWh US data, UK gap
key_risks.body: March 2026 kWh Analytics acquisition brings proprietary US renewable asset and loss databases (data_monitoring 3/4, pricing_modelling 3/4) to enhance Beazley's renewable pricing models. UK Lloyd's cedants get quantitative US-informed underwriting without disclosed UK curtailment telemetry or NESO-gate triggers — propagated non-firm intensity 2/4 (I=0.1031) applies without register-verified cedant connection status.

key_risks.title: Strong prep, tiny energy book
key_risks.body: Preparedness 75/100 and +24.5 margin-of-safety place Beazley in whitespace quadrant despite dedicated renewable underwriters (USD 75m offshore wind capacity, underwriting_expertise 3/4). Disclosed energy GWP is only 2% ($17.6m/$1.05bn) — capability via kWh and Arbol exceeds deployed UK grid premium; tenor mismatch 0/4 (5-year cover aligned to 5-year history) is a relative strength — tier: disclosed on tenor, assessed on prep gap.

key_risks.title: 18% marine-energy book
key_risks.body: Syndicate 33 discloses marine and energy GWP of USD 409m — 18% of USD 2.33bn total (book concentration effective 2/4; broad marine-energy line proxy). Merged energy and power teams offer USD 300m capacity with dedicated Power & Renewables underwriting. Exposed quadrant (exposure 66.0, margin-of-safety −26.0) — material energy franchise within Hiscox London Market, not a sideline class.

key_risks.title: Kao Harlow–Ark DC clustering
key_risks.body: Register-linked aggregation on two mapped assets (asset-kao-harlow, asset-ark) yields HHI 0.5 across east England and south-west boundaries — aggregation/correlation effective 3.7/4. DC blog research acknowledges data-centre power risk but trigger gap 4/4 and product fit 0/4: no parametric or availability product on energy pages. Descartes and Chaucer offer DC parametric structures Hiscox has not matched despite qualitative DC awareness.

key_risks.title: Traditional BI, low telemetry
key_risks.body: Data monitoring 1/4 and pricing modelling 1/4 — underwriting discipline focuses on attritional loss ratio management without published curtailment telemetry. AM Best A (capital 3/4) is adequate for the generalist energy book. Preparedness 40/100 on an 18% marine-energy franchise: capital and expertise do not close the physical-damage trigger gap on UK non-firm renewable and DC cedants.

key_risks.title: Parametric wind ≠ availability
key_risks.body: AXA XL discloses two non-damage products via AXA Climate (trigger_gap 2/4, product_fit 2/4) — wind and generation-index parametric covers for renewable revenue shortfall. Weather and production indices do not track NESO gate status or distribution curtailment orders; UK power cedants on Syndicate 2003 still face basis risk on grid-firmness losses despite being among the more parametric-ready carriers in batch4.

key_risks.title: Five-year cover, three-year history
key_risks.body: Disclosed max cover tenor 5 years vs 3 years claims history (tenor_mismatch 2/4, m=0.133) extends renewable policies beyond the UK constraint-loss record NESO publishes. AXICL Aero, Energy & Marine (14% segment, underwriting_expertise 3/4) writes on a tiny 2% energy GWP book (£27.8m/£1.38bn) — tail grid events may be underpriced relative to policy term on any UK non-firm cedant.

key_risks.title: Curtailment advice, no telemetry
key_risks.body: Risk consulting publishes curtailment loss-prevention analytics (data_monitoring 2/4, pricing_modelling 2/4) but AXA XL does not disclose in-house grid-availability telemetry comparable to parametric MGAs. Whitespace quadrant (+7.0 MoS, prep 65) on moderate exposure (58.0) — AA- capital (4/4, 224% SCR) supports advisory capability that monitoring tools do not match at portfolio level; tier: assessed.

key_risks.title: Near-zero disclosed energy GWP
key_risks.body: Syndicate 2488 accounts show energy GWP of GBP 0.37m — effectively 0% of GBP 727m total (book concentration effective 1/4 from blend). Trigger gap 4/4 and product fit 0/4 on UK energy pages: oil, gas and operational power on conventional physical-damage and BI wordings. Sidelined quadrant (margin-of-safety −16.2) — large diversified carrier with credible traditional energy but no NFRI-specific product lane.

key_risks.title: Traditional perils, no grid model
key_risks.body: Chubb UK energy risk engineering targets fire, machinery breakdown and nat-cat on power plant — not grid curtailment or data-centre availability (data monitoring 1/4, pricing modelling 1/4). Underwriting expertise 2/4 reflects global oil and gas leadership without public focus on UK non-firm grid connections or DC SLA risk. Aggregation/correlation effective 3.55/4 is portfolio-derived; Chubb's nat-cat accumulation framework does not model UK transmission constraint as a named PML.

key_risks.title: AA capital vs low preparedness
key_risks.body: S&P AA FSR (capital 4/4, disclosed) provides substantial headroom relative to the minimal UK energy tail. Preparedness 40/100 — the constraint is product and monitoring, not solvency. If Chubb expands UK renewable or DC underwriting on legacy triggers, AA-tier capital would absorb losses but basis risk on curtailment remains unpriced versus Chaucer or Descartes parametric offerings.

key_risks.title: Builders risk, not curtailment
key_risks.body: Zurich's Data Center Project Guard and 245+ data-centre projects in 2025 signal active UK/EU construction appetite (book_concentration 2/4), but disclosed non-damage product count is one construction-focused parametric (trigger_gap 3/4, product_fit 1/4). Operational grid curtailment and availability-index cover for energised DC and renewables clients remain absent — Descartes and Munich Re offer parametric structures Zurich does not match post-COD.

key_risks.title: Ten-year cover, three-year history
key_risks.body: Disclosed max cover tenor T=10y vs claims history H=3y yields tenor_mismatch 4/4 — the widest gap in batch7 L1 carriers. Long-dated DC and energy programmes underwritten today assume a curtailment-loss record that does not yet exist; pricing_modelling 2/4 covers construction-delay indices only, not NESO constraint dynamics.

key_risks.title: Culham–Latos register cluster
key_risks.body: Register-linked aggregation on two mapped assets (asset-latos-bridgend, asset-culham-aigz) yields HHI 0.5 across east England and southern boundaries — aggregation/correlation effective 3.7/4. Zurich's AI Growth Zone and Bridgend DC exposures concentrate on the same constrained export corridors without disclosed curtailment triggers.

key_risks.title: Index strength, grid blind spot
key_risks.body: Munich Re leads this batch on parametric readiness (trigger_gap 0/4, product_fit 4/4, four disclosed non-damage products) with EPEX/Speedwell wind indices and Statkraft QFI swap mechanics. Grid-status telemetry remains index-proxy rather than connection-register based (data_monitoring 3/4) — UK NESO boundary curtailment is not separately disclosed as a priced peril alongside weather volume indices.

key_risks.title: Seven-year tenor tail
key_risks.body: Disclosed max cover tenor is seven years against three years claims history (tenor_mismatch 3/4, m=0.27) — highest in batch16. Multi-year renewable hedges and proxy-revenue structures extend beyond evidenced UK curtailment loss history; AA-rated capital (298% SCR coverage) absorbs moderate stress but tail repricing on stacked UK cedants is not separately modelled.

key_risks.title: EUR 250m power concentration
key_risks.body: Power-and-utilities practice offers capacity up to EUR 250m addressing grid instability alongside renewable growth (book_concentration 3/4). Global Markets Syndicate renewable energy team further concentrates expertise — aggregation/correlation 2/4 on L3 portfolio proxy still implies correlated UK cedant exposure within a core named segment.

key_risks.title: Cloud SLA ≠ NESO curtailment
key_risks.body: Parametrix's four disclosed non-damage products (trigger gap 0/4) pay on cloud-provider SLA and availability-index triggers, not NESO gate status or distribution curtailment orders. UK DC cedants hedged on Parametrix downtime cover may still face basis risk when grid-firmness losses lack an insurable outage event — the MGA monitors 750+ data centres on provider telemetry, not constraint-register curtailment.

key_risks.title: Three-zone DC asset correlation
key_risks.body: Register-derived aggregation scores 4/4: MW-weighted HHI 0.3333 across three linked UK assets (Kao Harlow, Ark, Latos Bridgend) spanning east England, south-west and south Wales boundary zones. A correlated regional grid or cloud outage can trigger concurrent SLA claims on the specialist DC book — Parametrix Analytics models outage correlation on proprietary data, but linked-asset concentration exceeds typical diversified carrier books.

key_risks.title: Coverholder capacity opaque
key_risks.body: Lloyd's coverholder backed by A-rated insurers (capital 3/4) but precise aggregate capacity is not publicly disclosed. Book concentration 4/4 on DC/cloud availability means a correlated outage year could exhaust delegated limits before reinsurance responds — close via sfcr_mining on backing syndicates.

key_risks.title: Provisional yield parametric book
key_risks.body: Zero register blend — assessed renewable yield/revenue and NDBI lines with disclosed non-damage product architecture (trigger gap 0/4). Top exposure: book concentration 3/4, non-firm 3/4, aggregation 3/4. Tier label: assessed — close via register_pull on UK wind/solar cedant asset registers.

key_risks.title: Low-wind multi-cover trigger
key_risks.body: Descartes underwrites renewable yield and output shortfall on P50-indexed per-GWh triggers — non-firm intensity 3/4 on interruptible generation. Index covers on wind resource/yield are spatially correlated (aggregation 3/4): one UK low-wind period triggers multiple policies simultaneously. Parametric NDBI closes the physical-damage gap (0/4) but index basis risk remains vs site-level curtailment.

key_risks.title: Multi-year resilience tenor
key_risks.body: Descartes promotes multi-year parametric resilience structures (tenor mismatch 2/4) against relatively thin UK parametric-yield claims history. Tier-one capacity to $200m per policy (Munich Re, Swiss Re CS, AXA Climate) absorbs individual losses, but stacked multi-year yield covers on correlated indices extend tail beyond short experience window. Honest tier: assessed on tenor sub-factor.

key_risks.title: Aviva facility UK clustering
key_risks.body: Howden's Aviva-led Lloyd's-accredited renewables facility (up to £150m per declaration) concentrates UK wind/solar cedants across hub offices — book concentration 3/4 with partial aggregation 2/4. Interruptible-connection clients on the facility share correlated curtailment exposure even where capacity is spread across carriers.

key_risks.title: Damage facility vs parametric desk
key_risks.body: Core renewables facilities remain legacy damage-based BI, while Howden separately brokers parametric/non-damage cover (Instech case study) — trigger_gap 2/4. Clients on the £150m facility without a parametric top-up face absent availability and BI-without-damage triggers when curtailment hits without PD.

key_risks.title: Advisory data, no grid telemetry
key_risks.body: 160+ natural-resources specialists and due-diligence analytics (underwriting 4/4) but no proprietary grid telemetry — data monitoring 2/4. Multi-year project lifecycles vs annual placement (tenor mismatch 2/4) push curtailment modelling burden to carriers; close via register_pull on facility cedant ECR/TEC rows.

key_risks.title: Nimbus BI needs physical damage
key_risks.body: Marsh's Nimbus data-centre facility (~$2.7bn Jan 2026, incl. BI/DSU) ties business interruption to physical-damage perils — trigger_gap 2/4. Grid curtailment and off-site power availability loss without asset damage fall outside Nimbus triggers; DC clients on construction/DSU cover face absent availability and BI-without-damage gaps.

key_risks.title: $2.7bn DC construction stack
key_risks.body: Nimbus facility drives book concentration 3/4 on UK/EU data-centre construction pipeline via Global Digital Infrastructure team. Partial geographic diversification (aggregation 2/4) but hyperscale clusters in constraint zones concentrate cedant exposure — A-rated Lloyd's and company capacity ($2.7bn limit) absorb individual projects, not correlated curtailment.

key_risks.title: Energy integration, no curtailment model
key_risks.body: Risk engineering spans construction, energy integration and off-site power (data monitoring 3/4) but no dedicated curtailment modelling evidenced (pricing 2/4). Purpose-built Nimbus BI/DSU does not extend to ongoing operational grid firmness — close via register_pull on DC connection status and trigger_mining on energy-integration endorsements.

key_risks.title: Provisional DC franchise
key_risks.body: 0% filing-backed sub-factor weight — fully assessed profile. Top weighted lines: book concentration 3/4 (Digital Infrastructure Protector, Apr 2026), non-firm intensity 2/4 on grid-connected renewables, data monitoring 3/4. Close via register_pull on UK DC cedant connection status and trigger_mining on Protector wordings.

key_risks.title: Protector lacks curtailment trigger
key_risks.body: Digital Infrastructure Protector integrates construction-plus-operations cover (product fit 3/4) but no dedicated non-firm curtailment or availability product is evidenced — trigger gap 2/4. Standard physical-damage-led placements on power/utilities and DC clients leave basis risk when grid-connection losses lack insurable damage, lagging Marsh Nimbus on quantified dedicated capacity.

key_risks.title: DC-renewable book correlation
key_risks.body: Combined digital-infrastructure and renewable books correlate to constrained-grid regions (aggregation 2/4), partially offset by 140+ country footprint. UK solar-to-SMR supply chains and DC power dependencies share regional grid stress — several cedants could loss-hit concurrently without appearing in broker-level accumulation monitoring.

key_risks.title: Private-wire covers 56%, not night
key_risks.body: Downing Renewable Developments' 40 MW private-wire solar farm covers ~56% of current 71 MW IT load — at night, winter or high-demand periods the campus reverts to constrained East-of-England grid supply. Product fit 3/4 reflects engineering mitigation but does not eliminate curtailment basis risk on the grid-imported portion (trigger gap 2/4). Whitespace quadrant (60.6 exposure, 56.2 preparedness) — best-prepared asset in batch8.

key_risks.title: East England 15-year delay zone
key_risks.body: Harlow campus draws up to 150 MW expandable from UK Power Networks' East-of-England zone — flagged as a severe 15-year connection-delay region. Register-derived aggregation 3/4 on east_england boundary (HHI 1.0); connection firmness terms are not published. DNO ECR shows 3% flexible-connection share (non-firm compute exposure 0/4 measured) but regional constraint risk persists.

key_risks.title: Tenant SLA vs grid trigger
key_risks.body: Kao provides tenant power/availability SLAs for colocation clients — uncontracted curtailment on the grid-imported load creates business-loss exposure wider than standard PD/BI triggers (trigger gap 2/4). Infratil, Legal & General and Goldacre backing (capital 3/4) supports long-dated leases but no parametric grid-availability rider is evidenced. Close via trigger_mining on tenant SLA back-to-back insurance structures.

key_risks.title: MOD SLA outside BI
key_risks.body: Ark operates security-critical, MOD-adjacent infrastructure at Spring Park (~55 MW, Corsham) where government tenants require near-100% availability. A grid or mechanical failure triggering an SLA breach could incur contractual penalties and tenant migration costs — excluded from standard PD/BI wordings that require proximate physical damage (LMA BI guidance).

key_risks.title: M4 corridor multi-site correlation
key_risks.body: Ark's distributed UK estate spans the M4/Wiltshire corridor on the south-west transmission boundary (aggregation/correlation effective 3.4/4, HHI 1.0 single-zone). A regional grid fault or extreme weather event could simultaneously impact multiple campuses — property cat and BI programmes are structured per-site without explicit multi-site correlation caps.

key_risks.title: Diesel backup ≠ insurance trigger
key_risks.body: Campus-wide N+1 diesel (~33 generators at Spring Park) scores product_fit 3/4 as engineering resilience, not insurance cover — trigger_gap 1/4 reflects on-site backup but no parametric or availability product. Pricing_modelling 1/4; operational redundancy outruns trigger design for grid-lawful curtailment without equipment failure.

key_risks.title: Pre-revenue, no curtailment cover
key_risks.body: Latos launched 2024 with no publicly confirmed financial backers or demonstrated balance sheet (capital 1/4) — early-stage new entrant with no firm or curtailment-protected offtake evidenced (trigger gap 3/4). A curtailment or delay event at Bridgend with no insurance backstop falls entirely on the developer. Sidelined quadrant (53.7 exposure, 30.0 preparedness) — weakest preparedness in batch8.

key_risks.title: South Wales queue during reform
key_risks.body: Bridgend enters the GB demand-connection queue during NESO connections reform in a constrained South Wales distribution zone — aggressive 40-site build-to-2030 plan vs uncertain grid capacity and connection timing (tenor mismatch 3/4). Cardiff flagship cites Tremorfa Energy Park BESS partnership but Bridgend equivalent is unconfirmed (product fit 2/4). No live SCADA or curtailment telemetry (data monitoring 1/4).

key_risks.title: 40-site ambition, thin depth
key_risks.body: Latos plans 40 facilities by 2030 with a 90 MVA Cardiff flagship plus smaller Edge sites — book concentration 2/4 at portfolio level but financial depth is not publicly demonstrated at investment-grade levels. Register-derived aggregation 3/4 on south_wales boundary (HHI 1.0). Absent trigger: parametric grid availability and delay-in-startup for queue-related energisation slip.

key_risks.title: 500 MW needs undelivered grid
key_risks.body: Culham selected for dual-resilient 132kV/400kV grid with ~100 MW confirmed spare capacity, but expansion toward 500 MW peak requires additional network reinforcement not yet delivered (book_concentration 4/4, tenor_mismatch 3/4). Scale-up tranches beyond ~200 MW enter infirm-connection territory — capacity derating without equipment failure (dominant channel: capacity derating).

key_risks.title: Operator TBD — cover unplaced
key_risks.body: UKAEA-led AI Growth Zone with expression-of-interest process underway to select a strategic investor/operator — insurance programme ownership, declared values and commercial PD/BI placement remain unallocated during procurement. Government entities may self-insure or use Crown Cover with different terms from commercial parametric or availability products.

key_risks.title: Firm tranche, latent trigger
key_risks.body: Initial 100 MW tranche has firm-connection backing (non_firm_compute_exposure 0/4 on TEC register) and dual-resilient feeds score product_fit 3/4 — but trigger_gap 2/4 reflects no availability or parametric cover for upper-tranche curtailment once reinforcement slips. Zurich maps this asset in its register-linked book (HHI 0.5 with Latos Bridgend).

key_risks.title: Weather parametric ≠ curtailment
key_risks.body: Swiss Re Corporate Solutions markets the first UK red-weather-warning parametric policy (Willis partnership) and four disclosed non-damage products (trigger gap 0/4). Weather-index triggers capture meteorological events, not NESO gate status or distribution curtailment orders — UK power/DC cedants hedged on Met Office warnings may still face basis risk on grid-firmness losses.

key_risks.title: Diversified book hides UK DC tail
key_risks.body: Broad multi-line book dilutes single-grid correlation (aggregation 1/4, book concentration 2/4). UK power and data-centre cedants are secondary to the renewable-energy and parametric weather franchise — correlated UK DC stress may be immaterial at group level but invisible in cedant-level monitoring until renewals.

key_risks.title: AA- parent, assessed cedant mix
key_risks.body: Swiss Re Group AA- rating (capital 4/4) and 100/100 preparedness provide ample margin-of-safety 71.2, but only 20% of sub-factors are filing-backed. Non-firm intensity 1/4 is assessed — UK DC cedant connection status on assumed treaties is not register-verified.

key_risks.title: 0.15% energy GWP disclosed
key_risks.body: SCOR Syndicate disclosed energy/power GWP share of 0.15% (£0.538m of £356m) — book concentration 0/4. UK power and DC cedants are incidental to the global book; latent rating 2/4 suggests underwriting interest exceeds disclosed premium. Provisional tier: disclosed share may understate Lloyd's energy panel participation.

key_risks.title: Parametric thought, treaty gap
key_risks.body: Alternative Solutions team builds weather-index structures (trigger gap 1/4, product fit 3/4) including wind-index windfarm revenue cover, but standard energy treaties remain physical-damage led. UK cedants without parametric extensions face residual basis risk on non-damage curtailment relative to Munich Re or Nephila.

key_risks.title: A+ capital, negligible UK tail
key_risks.body: S&P A+ parent support (capital 3/4) and globally diversified book (aggregation 1/4) mean UK grid-constraint PML is immaterial to group solvency. Risk is opportunity cost — SCOR may underwrite UK DC cedants on legacy triggers without pricing the non-firm tail competitors are building parametric products for.

key_risks.title: European renewables UK correlation
key_risks.body: Hannover Re's energy and engineering segment scores aggregation/correlation 2/4 with explicit UK power correlation within a broader European portfolio. Offshore wind, solar, BESS and data-centre cedants under CMP434/435 connections reform create mixed firm/non-firm exposure (non-firm intensity 2/4). A significant UK grid-constraint event could produce correlated claims across multiple European cedants Hannover assumes.

key_risks.title: Parametric capability, treaty PD dominance
key_risks.body: Hannover's parametric solutions practice (trigger gap 1/4, product fit 3/4) can structure index-triggered reinsurance, but standard energy treaties remain physical-damage dominated. UK cedants on annual PD-led covers face partial basis risk when curtailment losses lack damage — parametric capability exists but is not the default ceded structure.

key_risks.title: Project-finance tenor mismatch
key_risks.body: Multi-year treaties and project-finance-linked energy structures (tenor mismatch 2/4) extend cover against near-zero UK non-firm curtailment loss history. AA- S&P rating and capital 4/4 provide headroom, but long-dated structured covers on BESS and DC campus build-outs carry model risk on thin comparable experience.

key_risks.title: Cat aggregation masks grid events
key_risks.body: RenaissanceRe's property-cat-led specialty book scores aggregation/correlation 2/4, but accumulation models target named nat-cat perils rather than man-made grid-infrastructure events. UK power-curtailment correlation is not a modelled scenario for the dominant cat franchise — several energy cedants could loss-hit concurrently without appearing in RDS-style energy accumulation.

key_risks.title: Parametric gap vs cat peers
key_risks.body: Trigger gap 2/4 with only two disclosed non-damage products; product fit 2/4. Specialty marine/energy includes renewables but availability-index structures lag Nephila or Swiss Re Corporate Solutions. UK cedants on physical-damage-led RenRe treaties face basis risk when curtailment losses lack insurable damage — legacy wording leaves more spillover than parametric competitors.

key_risks.title: Provisional UK energy slice
key_risks.body: 20% sub-factor weight disclosed; book concentration 1/4 and non-firm intensity 1/4 are assessed. RenRe's UK power/DC cedant share is not filing-quantified. A+ capital (4/4) comfortably covers the inferred minor energy tail, but underwriting action on emerging UK DC cedants relies on specialist judgment rather than register evidence.

key_risks.title: Offshore-heavy PD trigger gap
key_risks.body: Arch Re scores trigger gap 3/4 with a single disclosed non-damage product and product fit 1/4 — among the weakest parametric profiles in this batch. Energy cedants are upstream offshore and conventional power on firm connections; UK data-centre and renewable cedants with non-firm links are negligible today but inherit physical-damage treaty wordings that exclude pure availability losses.

key_risks.title: Nat-cat models, not grid PML
key_risks.body: Arch Analytics focuses on RMS/AIR nat-cat perils; energy pricing is experience-rated without documented curtailment telemetry. Aggregation/correlation 1/4 reflects geographic diversification, but accumulation targets hurricane and earthquake scenarios — a UK transmission constraint event would not appear in Arch's dominant property-cat PML framework.

key_risks.title: A+ capital vs sidelined prep
key_risks.body: AM Best A+ (disclosed) gives capital 4/4 — deep balance sheet relative to the minor UK power tail (book concentration 1/4). Margin-of-safety 22.5 reflects low preparedness (55/100) not capital strain. The risk is mispricing emerging UK DC cedants on legacy triggers, not solvency under a grid shock.

key_risks.title: DC-renewable correlation stack
key_risks.body: Nephila Climate backs weather-linked proxy revenue for data-centre offtakers (Iron Mountain, Microsoft) alongside wind/solar swap positions. A UK grid-constraint or regional low-wind event can hit multiple ceded structures in the same quarter — aggregation/correlation scores 3/4. Collateralised ILS capacity absorbs individual losses, but correlated weather–curtailment episodes are not separately capital-modelled.

key_risks.title: Provisional cedant UK mix
key_risks.body: Only 10% of sub-factor weight is filing-backed (trigger_gap disclosed; remainder assessed). Exposure axis 61/100 rests on proxy-generation and DC procurement deals without syndicate-level UK cedant registers. Top assessed lines: non-firm intensity (3/4), book concentration (3/4), aggregation/correlation (3/4). Tier label: assessed — close via register_pull and sfcr_mining on Markel/Nephila collateral reports.

key_risks.title: Capital vs correlated tail
key_risks.body: Markel-backed collateralised capacity (capital 3/4) supports individual deal sizing but sits below Munich Re or Swiss Re AA-tier depth. Multi-year proxy revenue swaps (tenor mismatch 2/4) extend against thin UK curtailment history — tail scenarios on stacked DC–renewable hedges may exceed per-deal collateral if several UK cedants reprice simultaneously.

key_risks.title: Provisional evidence base
key_risks.body: Only 0% of sub-factor weight rests on registers or filings. Exposure axis 0% measured · preparedness 0%. Largest assessed lines: Book concentration (assessed, w=0.30), Non-firm intensity (assessed, w=0.25), Data & monitoring (assessed, w=0.25). Close via book_mining / sfcr_mining · register_pull.

key_risks.title: Trigger gap — non-damage losses
key_risks.body: Trigger gap scores 3.0/4 (disclosed). Filing-backed product count only — wording detail still thin. Curtailment and availability losses may not match physical-damage wordings on the binder.

key_risks.title: Aggregation / correlation concentration
key_risks.body: Aggregation / correlation at 2.0/4 (assessed). Reinsurer tail sits on correlated UK power / DC cedant stacks — HHI rises when boundaries align. Fidelis Re's specialty portfolio includes energy, political risk and property, which limits the UK power accumulation to a sub-segment. Hard-to-place energy ris

key_risks.title: Two BI products, no availability
key_risks.body: Allianz Commercial discloses two non-damage/parametric products (trigger_gap 2/4, product_fit 2/4) via expert BI articles, but neither is an availability-index or NESO-gate trigger for UK power cedants. Strategic Energy & Construction franchise (book_concentration 3/4 assessed) writes damage/BI on renewables and utilities — curtailment losses without physical damage still face basis risk versus Swiss Re Corporate Solutions red-weather parametric.

key_risks.title: Strong prep, unmodelled grid tail
key_risks.body: Preparedness 80/100 and AA group capital (4/4) give +14.8 margin-of-safety on earning_it quadrant, but aggregation/correlation 3/4 (portfolio HHI 0.9348) is register-derived not filing-quantified at cedant level. Allianz Risk Consulting exceeds generic statistics (data_monitoring 3/4) yet publishes no UK curtailment telemetry — correlated constraint episodes may be immaterial at group level but invisible until renewals.

key_risks.title: Scenario tools, no curtailment model
key_risks.body: Technical risk consulting and scenario tools on large industrial risks (pricing_modelling 3/4 assessed) exceed rule-of-thumb pricing but stop short of validated curtailment-probability methodology for UK renewables. Tenor mismatch 2/4 (5-year cover vs 3-year claims history) extends exposure against thin UK constraint-loss history — tier: assessed.

key_risks.title: 16% energy, zero parametric
key_risks.body: Aviva GCS discloses 16% energy GWP (£52m/£317m via Probitas syndicate stamp) on renewables construction-through-operational programmes with zero non-damage products (trigger_gap 4/4, product_fit 0/4). Exposed quadrant at −25.5 margin-of-safety — among the highest grid-relevant book concentrations in batch14 writing damage/BI only on UK wind, solar and BESS cedants.

key_risks.title: Seven-year cover, three-year history
key_risks.body: Disclosed max cover tenor 7 years vs 3 years claims history (tenor_mismatch 3/4, m=0.267) extends renewable policies beyond the UK constraint-loss record NESO publishes. Named UK Renewable Energy team underwrites on engineering experience (pricing_modelling 1/4 assessed) without curtailment-probability models — tail grid events may be underpriced relative to policy term.

key_risks.title: HHI proxy on concentrated book
key_risks.body: Register-derived aggregation/correlation 3/4 (HHI 0.9348 over 46 L3 assets) combined with propagated non-firm intensity 2/4 (I=0.1031) flags correlated UK constraint zones on a book where cedant-level connection status is not filing-verified. key_risks.title: Winter solar import exposure
key_risks.body: Brightwell 8 MW private-wire solar supplies ~50% of annual campus energy and up to 90% on peak summer days — winter and evening NOC load relies entirely on grid import (~11 MVA allocated). Lawful curtailment on telco operational DC load would not trigger standard BI (trigger_gap 3/4); no parametric cover bridges seasonal grid-import dependency.

key_risks.title: 11→40 MVA on one node
key_risks.body: Single 100-acre campus hosting BT's main R&D site, Network Operations Centre and operational DC load on one Martlesham Primary allocation — UKPN documents flag potential growth to 40 MVA (book_concentration 3/4, aggregation/correlation effective 3.6/4). Property cat aggregates at site; grid-system curtailment correlation rarely priced.

key_risks.title: NOC telemetry, no trigger
key_risks.body: Network Operations Centre and intelligent PDU monitoring score data_monitoring 3/4 — above generic telco benchmarks — but product_fit 2/4 reflects on-site solar mitigation only, not insurance availability cover. Pricing_modelling 1/4; strong operational monitoring outruns trigger design for grid-lawful curtailment.

key_risks.title: Docklands curtailment, no damage
key_risks.body: Fully operational DR facility running ~3.5 MVA load on ten-year lease through 2029 — Docklands grid demand growth could trigger lawful curtailment without damage to insured plant (trigger_gap 3/4). Standard PD/BI wordings do not respond; curtailment is not a proximate physical-damage event under LMA BI guidance.

key_risks.title: Isle of Dogs neighbour stack
key_risks.body: Single dedicated 34,875 sq ft facility on Greenwich View estate alongside multiple neighbouring data-centre buildings sharing local power infrastructure — aggregation/correlation effective 3.8/4 (HHI 1.0). Correlated outage or curtailment hits full DR value; book_concentration 3/4 on one operational node.

key_risks.title: 2029 lease reversion gap
key_risks.body: Savills auction listing documents Bloomberg occupation on lease through 2029 — insurance programme continuity, declared values and grid-connection assignment at reversion are undisclosed. Operational PD/BI may lapse or reprice at lease event; no curtailment product evidenced in either period (product_fit 1/4).

key_risks.title: 1.2 GW on 1 GW export
key_risks.body: Each phase holds a secured 1 GW grid connection but may install up to 1.2 GW — operational curtailment whenever turbine output exceeds the export limit (trigger_gap 3/4). Forewind modelling optimises annual yield but guarantees routine curtailment at the onshore substation; lost MWh not recoverable under damage-only BI or CfD revenue stack.

key_risks.title: 3.6 GW phased aggregation
key_risks.body: World's largest offshore wind complex at 3.6 GW across three 1.2 GW phases — phases A and B share the Creyke Beck 400 kV export point while phase C uses Lackenby, creating correlated curtailment at two adjacent onshore nodes (aggregation/correlation effective 3.8/4, book_concentration 4/4).

key_risks.title: SCADA depth, zero parametric
key_risks.body: Utility-scale offshore SCADA with HVDC telemetry scores data_monitoring 3/4 and capital_reinsurance 4/4 (SSE, Equinor, Vårgrønn project finance) — but product_fit 0/4 with no curtailment or parametric insurance at asset level. Pricing_modelling 1/4; merchant upside eroded by overplanting curtailment without insurable trigger.

key_risks.title: BM payments ≠ availability cover
key_risks.body: Hornsea One (1.2 GW) and Hornsea Two (1.3 GW) receive documented Balancing Mechanism constraint payments at £164–£201/MWh to reduce output — Ofgem monitors TCLC compliance but BM compensation is not parametric availability cover against revenue loss (trigger gap 3/4). Standard property/BI requires proximate physical damage; curtailment economics sit outside the trigger. Product fit 0/4 — no asset-level curtailment insurance evidenced.

key_risks.title: 2.5 GW Yorkshire Round 3 stack
key_risks.body: ~2.5 GW offshore generation concentrates in one Yorkshire Round 3 zone exporting via National Grid's east-coast corridor — book concentration 4/4 and aggregation 3/4 (HHI 1.0). Correlated constraint exposure with other North Sea wind connects; a single boundary event suppresses output across the full Hornsea stack. Ørsted capital 4/4 provides balance-sheet headroom but does not close the non-damage trigger gap.

key_risks.title: CfD tenor vs constraint regime
key_risks.body: Multi-decade CfD-backed assets face a worsening constraint-payment regime as more North Sea wind connects (tenor mismatch 3/4). Full offshore SCADA documents high-volume BM constraint dispatch (data monitoring 3/4) but insurance programmes have not kept pace with escalating curtailment frequency. Exposed quadrant (80.2 exposure, 47.5 preparedness).

key_risks.title: EC5 export until reinforcement
key_risks.body: NESO East Anglia Network Study models EC5 as a thermal export limit — as TWO/THREE/ONE North connect, generators behind the boundary face increasing constraint payments rather than full merchant export (non_firm_intensity 3/4, 74% flexible TEC share). Constraint payments partially offset lost revenue but are not insurance; damage-only BI does not respond.

key_risks.title: 3.9 GW hub single zone
key_risks.body: East Anglia Hub clusters over 3.9 GW across four projects (ONE operational, TWO/THREE/ONE North building) in one southern North Sea zone converging on the EC5 export boundary — aggregation/correlation effective 3.8/4, book_concentration 4/4. Correlated constraint risk grows as later phases energise; margin_of_safety −41.5, quadrant exposed.

key_risks.title: GBP 10bn, zero parametric
key_risks.body: GBP 10 bn multi-phase hub financing with 30+ year asset life (tenor_mismatch 4/4) but product_fit 0/4 — no evidence of curtailment or parametric insurance at asset level. East Anglia ONE runs full offshore SCADA (data_monitoring 3/4) yet trigger_gap 3/4 leaves merchant revenue loss from lawful curtailment outside standard operational programmes.

key_risks.title: Undispatched peaker revenue gap
key_risks.body: Keadby 2 holds 893 MW transmission entry with a 15-year Capacity Market agreement but earns variable merchant revenue only when dispatched — prolonged low-demand or high-renewable periods suppress income without plant damage (trigger gap 3/4). No evidenced availability or parametric cover for merchant/Capacity Market revenue volatility. Exposed quadrant (75.5 exposure, 52.5 preparedness) — flexible generation role offsets but does not insure revenue gaps.

key_risks.title: Shared 400 kV Keadby node
key_risks.body: Keadby 1 (732 MW) and Keadby 2 (893 MW) share one 400 kV National Grid connection area at the Humber cluster — book concentration 3/4 and aggregation 2/4. A transmission fault or substation incident hits both units concurrently; physical damage may be insured but correlated dispatch suppression is not. SSE Thermal capital 4/4 (FTSE-listed SSE plc) provides GBP 350m Keadby 2 investment headroom.

key_risks.title: TEC Gate 71% flexible zone
key_risks.body: NESO TEC Gate shows 71% flexible-connection share across 27 register rows in the Humber constraint zone (non-firm intensity 3/4 measured). Siemens Energy 9000HL turbine with 30-minute ramp (data monitoring 3/4) supports grid balancing dispatch but insurance product fit remains 1/4. Tenor mismatch 2/4 as 15-year Capacity Market contract partially offsets long asset life.

key_risks.title: Pre-build connection slip
key_risks.body: DCO granted September 2024 with a National Grid 600 MW connection offer but no public Gate 1/2 firmness confirmation under NESO's reformed connections regime — construction versus energisation timing risk (tenor_mismatch 4/4). Pre-build greenfield with trigger_gap 4/4: no availability or parametric cover for connection delay or curtailment risk.

key_risks.title: Cottam corridor NSIP stack
key_risks.body: Up to 600 MW solar plus 600 MW BESS across four parcels converges on a single 400 kV point of connection at the former Cottam coal substation — aggregation/correlation 4/4, book_concentration 4/4. Shares the corridor with neighbouring Gate Burton and other NSIPs; correlated constraint risk across co-located projects rarely priced in property cat.

key_risks.title: 40-year asset, zero cover
key_risks.body: 40-year NSIP asset horizon (margin_of_safety −46.2, quadrant exposed) against product_fit 1/4 and data_monitoring 1/4 — no operational curtailment history and no evidence of availability or parametric protection in the document library. Infirm connection may cap export below 1,200 MW nameplate without equipment failure.

key_risks.title: B4 boundary, firm but curtailed
key_risks.body: 882 MW Moray West holds firm SSEN Transmission connection but B4 Scottish boundary constrained 42% of hours in 2025 per Modo Energy — constraint Balancing Mechanism payments are not availability or parametric cover against revenue loss (trigger gap 3/4, product fit 0/4). Full offshore SCADA documents high-volume BM constraint dispatch (data monitoring 3/4). Exposed quadrant (71.2 exposure, 42.5 preparedness).

key_risks.title: Moray East-West correlated cluster
key_risks.body: Moray West (882 MW, 60×14.7 MW turbines) sits alongside Moray East on the Moray Firth B4/B6 export corridor — maximal aggregation 4/4 and book concentration 4/4. A single boundary constraint event suppresses output across the co-located offshore cluster without turbine damage. Ocean Winds JV capital 3/4 (EDP Renewables / ENGIE) with GBP 800m+ Scottish economic commitment.

key_risks.title: CfD vs Scottish curtailment trend
key_risks.body: Multi-decade CfD-backed asset against rapidly worsening Scottish boundary curtailment costs (tenor mismatch 4/4). NESO TEC Gate shows 2% flexible-connection share in the register zone (non-firm intensity 0/4 measured) — firm connection does not eliminate systemic B4 constraint. Absent trigger: parametric grid availability indexed to boundary constraint hours.

key_risks.title: Autobidder revenue, no NDBI
key_risks.body: 7.5 MW/15 MWh Tesla Megapack BESS at Holes Bay earns merchant, FFR and Balancing Mechanism revenues via Autobidder — constraint or balancing de-dispatch can suppress trading income without equipment failure (trigger gap 4/4). Standard property/BI responds only to physical damage; no evidenced parametric dispatch-shortfall or NDBI cover on FRV/Harmony disclosures. Tier label: assessed — close via trigger_mining on operational programme wordings.

key_risks.title: Single Dorset distribution node
key_risks.body: All 7.5 MW sits behind one SSEN distribution connection at Holes Bay, Poole — book concentration 3/4 and register-derived aggregation 3/4 (HHI 1.0 on unknown boundary). A local constraint, substation fault or distribution outage hits the full asset value in one event; non-damage node economics remain outside standard PD limits. Close via register_pull on SSEN connection firmness terms.

key_risks.title: Long-life asset, volatile merchant
key_risks.body: Commissioned June 2020 with a long infrastructure horizon against a short and volatile BESS merchant revenue history (tenor mismatch 3/4). Autobidder SCADA provides strong telemetry (data monitoring 3/4) but no insurance pricing methodology is disclosed at asset level. Exposed quadrant (76.5 exposure, 42.5 preparedness) — tail risk is trigger structure, not operator balance sheet.

key_risks.title: Creyke Beck cluster stack
key_risks.body: 49.9 MW/98 MWh Phase 2 tranche (NESO TEC PRO-001906, Built January 2023) concentrates maximal book concentration 4/4 and aggregation 4/4 at one Creyke Beck GSP — shared with Pillswood Phase 1 and Dogger Bank export corridor. A constraint or transmission fault at the node suppresses revenue across correlated assets without turbine or battery damage. Highest exposure score in batch8 (91.3) — exposed quadrant.

key_risks.title: Autobidder dispatch, no parametric
key_risks.body: Tesla Megapack 2-hour system with Autobidder SCADA earns spread and Balancing Mechanism dispatch — constraint or balancing de-dispatch cuts trading revenue without equipment failure (trigger gap 4/4). No public evidence of availability or parametric curtailment cover; standard property/BI remains damage-triggered. Phase 2 ranked among GB's top-performing BESS assets on telemetry (data monitoring 3/4) but insurance product fit is 1/4.

key_risks.title: TEC Gate 63% non-firm zone
key_risks.body: NESO TEC Gate register shows 63% flexible-connection share across 51 rows in the constraint zone (non-firm intensity 3/4 measured). Firm TEC entry on Phase 2 does not eliminate systemic boundary constraint — revenue volatility from dispatch suppression sits outside standard BI wordings. Tenor mismatch 3/4 as January 2023 energisation outruns curtailment loss history.

key_risks.title: 680 MW non-firm dispatch gap
key_risks.body: 680 MW / 1,360 MWh BESS at Trafford Carrington connects non-firm at National Grid's 400 kV Carrington substation — balancing de-dispatch or constraint orders cut merchant and Statkraft-guaranteed revenue without plant damage (trigger_gap 4/4, non_firm_intensity 3/4). No evidenced dispatch-deviation or NDBI cover on the £235m pre-COD finance package. Exposed quadrant (87.5 exposure, 41.2 preparedness).

key_risks.title: Maximal Manchester node concentration
key_risks.body: One of the UK's largest BESS projects — full 680 MW behind a single Carrington 400 kV transmission point with ENWL infrastructure on associated Trafford land (aggregation_correlation 4/4, book_concentration 4/4). A boundary constraint or node outage correlates the entire 1.36 GWh insured stack. Close via register_pull on National Grid Carrington firmness letter.

key_risks.title: Finance tenor, zero COD history
key_risks.body: Financial close November 2025 with £235m debt syndicate and energisation targeted late 2027 — long project-finance tenor against zero operating curtailment record (tenor_mismatch 4/4). CAR/ALOP may exist on build but post-energisation dispatch suppression remains uninsured. Close via trigger_mining on lender non-damage extension requirements.

key_risks.title: B5 de-dispatch without damage
key_risks.body: 500 MW/1 GWh BESS at Broken Cross sited on the B5 Scottish boundary to absorb curtailed wind — FID early 2026, COD targeted late 2027. B5 boundary constraints can force BESS de-dispatch without equipment damage; merchant and BM revenue loss sits outside damage-only property cover (trigger_gap 3/4, margin_of_safety −50.0).

key_risks.title: Coalburn 1+2 co-location
key_risks.body: Very large single site on one constrained Scottish B5 transmission boundary, co-located with Coalburn 1 (500 MW/1 GWh) — aggregation/correlation 4/4 (HHI 1.0), book_concentration 4/4. Single-boundary correlated curtailment hits both phases; CIP portfolio concentration not separately capital-modelled for constraint de-dispatch.

key_risks.title: Zero BESS availability product
key_risks.body: Product_fit 0/4 and pricing_modelling 0/4 — no availability or parametric curtailment product identified; revenue hedging through merchant, capacity market and SSE offtake does not transfer grid-firmness risk. Underwriting_expertise 0/4 at asset level; CIP and AIP are investors, not risk carriers.
